titulo: Humanoids in Oct 2026: demo, pilot, and production
lead: Humanoid videos are everywhere; robots delivered to paying customers, not so much. Before you open any model, you learn to tell demo, pilot, and production apart with a source and a date, to read a humanoid's price without falling for an old number, and to recognize the platforms a lab can buy today.
objetivo: classify 6 humanoids as demo, pilot, or production, each with a source and a date, without repeating an outdated price or model.

aprende.t: The three stages and the evidence each one requires
Who is where in Oct 2026: Figure, Atlas, Optimus, Unitree, 1X, Booster
Why the G1 doesn't have a single price
The 6-robot table and the script that checks source and date

hero_alt: Dark warehouse aisle with a humanoid robot carrying a box in the background and a clipboard in the foreground.

secoes.titulo: From video to robot in series
secoes.sub: Each step asks for stronger evidence. Click to see who is at each one in Oct 2026.

nos.detalhe: There is only video, a stage, or pre-sale. The Optimus V3 had not been shown in public until Aug 2026; Tesla promises production start before the end of 2026 in an SEC filing. The 1X NEO is in pre-sale (US$ 20k) and the factory has been producing since 04/30/2026, but delivery to customers was not confirmed (reported, 07/2026).

Works at a customer, on a narrow task, in small numbers. Figure 03 (launched in 10/2025) with Helix 02 (01/27/2026) reached BMW Spartanburg around 06/2026; the production Atlas debuted at CES 2026 with the 2026 batch committed to Hyundai and Google DeepMind; Digit moves boxes at GXO. All reported by the press.

Sold at a public price to whoever pays. Unitree lists the G1 (US$ 13.5k for the base), R1 (US$ 4,900 / 5,900), and H2 (US$ 29,900) in its official store; Booster sells the K1 also through the RoboCup 2026 program. This is the step of research platforms.

Thousands per year. Unitree reportedly shipped 5,511 humanoids in 2025 and went public on the STAR market on 08/19/2026; UBTech has been delivering the Walker S2 since 11/2025 and aims for 5,000 per year in 2026. Both reported, with no independent audit.

secoes.legenda: Mark the lowest stage your source supports. A pretty video doesn't move anyone up a step.
secoes.dica: Facts marked "reported" come from the press or an aggregator; those from an official store were read on 10/19/2026.

secoes.titulo: Four traps for anyone reading the market

texto: The base G1 costs US$ 13.5k in the Unitree store, but it comes without secondary development: with no SDK, it's no good for research. The EDU, which is, is sold on request; resellers cite US$ 43.5k to 73.9k (reported).
In the RoboCup 2026 program, the competition version has a public price of US$ 35k. That's three products with the same name.

exemplo.texto: Base G1: US$ 13,500, no SDK (unitree.com/g1, read on 10/19/2026). EDU: on request; price varies by version and reseller.

texto: Material from 2024–25 still talks about Figure 01 and 02 with "GPT-4 built in." Today it's the Figure 03, with Helix 02 controlling the whole body (the low-level controller runs at 1 kHz, according to Figure).
The hydraulic Atlas was retired; the product Atlas is electric and debuted at CES 2026.
K-Scale Labs, which sold the open K-Bot, shut down in 11/2025 and open-sourced the rest of the project (reported). Don't recommend it as a vendor.

Cheap platforms that exist: Unitree R1 (US$ 5,900), Booster K1 (95 cm, 22 degrees of freedom), Berkeley Humanoid Lite (under US$ 5k in parts, reported) and ToddlerBot (30 degrees of freedom, public parts list).

The Beijing humanoid half marathon (04/19/2026) was won in 50:26 by an autonomous robot, versus 2:40:42 in 2025; the World Humanoid Robot Games in August 2026 brought together about 2,056 robots (reported).
A record shows progress in locomotion, not that the robot works in a factory. Market and funding rounds are covered in the VLA course.

Unitree G1             falta: estágio, fonte, data
  Unitree R1             falta: estágio, fonte, data
  Booster K1             falta: estágio, fonte, data
  Figure 03              falta: estágio, fonte, data

The empty table fails: 0 of 6 and exit code 1. That's how the criterion fails before the work is done.

abas.rot: Common mistake: "coming soon" and a video as a source
abas.html:
Tesla Optimus V3       falta: estágio, fonte, data
estágios: demo 0 · piloto 0 · produção 0
1 robôs, 0 com fonte e data
saída: 1

"Coming soon" is not a stage, "I saw it in a video" is not a URL, and "2026" alone is not a date. For the Optimus V3, the honest answer is demo, with Tesla's source and the date.

secoes.sub: Open ~/fth/fichas.csv and fill in the stage, the source (https://), the date and the evidence in a few words. The sources are in the diagram, in the traps and in the links at the end of the lesson.

6 robôs, 6 com fonte e data

One possible answer, with the sources from this lesson. You can disagree on a stage (is the Atlas already production?), as long as the evidence backs it up.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after you answer.

perguntas.p: A lab wants the Unitree G1 to write its own controller. Which version works?
opcoes: The US$ 13.5k base, the cheapest in the store.
The EDU, sold on request, which comes with the SDK.
Any of them: the SDK is the same in all.
perguntas.explica: The base comes without secondary development (no SDK). To program the robot, the version is the EDU, on request. The price depends on the version and the reseller.

perguntas.p: A company posts a video of the robot folding clothes and opens pre-orders. Which stage does the evidence support?
opcoes: Production, because there is already a public price in the store.
Pilot, because customers are paying a deposit on the pre-order.
Demo, until delivery to a customer is confirmed.
Scale, because the factory is already producing.
perguntas.explica: Pre-orders and a video are still a demo. Pilot requires the robot working at a customer; production requires serial delivery to paying buyers. That is the case of the 1X NEO in 2026.

perguntas.p: Which of these sentences can go into material from Oct/2026 without a caveat?
opcoes: The Optimus V3 was shown to the public in the 1st quarter of 2026, as planned.
The Figure 03 is already sold to consumers on Figure's official website.
The base G1 comes with an SDK and costs US$ 13.5k in the Unitree store.
Unitree lists the R1 from US$ 4,900 (official store, 10/19/2026).
perguntas.explica: Only the R1 one has a primary source and a date. The Optimus V3 had not appeared in public until Aug/2026, the Figure 03 has no consumer sales, and the base G1 comes without an SDK.

perguntas.p: The 2026 Beijing half marathon was won in 50:26. What does that number prove?
opcoes: That humanoids already work full shifts in factories.
That autonomous locomotion has advanced a lot in one year.
That the winning robot is for sale.
That running and manipulation are at the same level.
perguntas.explica: In 2025 the time was 2:40:42. The jump shows locomotion, not useful work or a product for sale. A record is a showcase; a product's stage is proven by delivery.

itens.texto: Demo, pilot, production, scale: mark the lowest step the source supports.
Always with version, source, and date; the base G1 has no SDK.
Figure 01/02, K-Scale, and the G1 at 16k are from before 2026.
